newsitem.title: USA: IPL says power outage takes out 1 mmbpd.
newsitem.headline: IPL says power outage takes out 1 mmbpd.

text.p: Interprovincial Pipe Line Inc said Monday that a power outage in Minnesota has hit three of its pumping stations and taken out one million barrels per day of throughput.
"IPL stations in Minnesota at Viking, Plummer and Clearbrook have been without power since late Saturday, around 2335 Mountain Standard Time," said Alan Roth, a spokesman for IPL.
"That has shut lines 2b, three and 13; we're estimating about a million barrels a day" of lost throughput, he said.
The pipeline had been carrying about 1.4 million barrels a day.

"Without those pumping stations you lose the correct pressure and velocitiy and if you do that you could end up with degradation (of the crude)," Roth added. It will probably be Wednesday at the earliest that the pumping stations can resume operations, depending on the situation with the power outage.
He said the latest information he had was that only 25 of 150 Minnesota communities had had power restored as of early Monday.

Line 2 runs 1,098 miles from Edmonton, capital of Canada's Alberta province to Superior, Michigan and carries light, medium and synthetic crudes plus condensate. Line 3 also runs from Edmonton to Superior and carries light, medium, heavy and synthetic crudes plus condensate.
Line 13 runs 800 miles from Hardisty, Alberta (downstream from Edmonton) to Clearbrook, Minn. and carries light crude.

Roth said Line six, running from Superior to Sarnia via Chicago (759 miles), which carries light, medium, heavy, synthetic crudes and consensate, was shut down on Sunday morning due to short inventories.

"However, there are enough inventories in Superior to keep line five operating for several days," he said. Line five runs from Superior to Sarnia, Ont. via north of Lake Michigan (645 miles) carries NGLs, light and synthetic crude, condensate.
Also, line one from Edmonton to Superior, Wis. (1,098 miles), which carries NGLs, products and synthetic crudes, gets some supplies from lines two and 13, Roth said.
